_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the CRM roadmap rendered at /crm/roadmap. Task `status` is maintained AUTOMATICALLY by `npm run roadmap:crm` (scripts/gen-roadmap.mjs), which inspects the real extension source tree and flips a task to `done` when everything in its `detect` block exists. The CRM grows out of the Newsletter / Subscriber CRM (renamed to `crm` and reorganized), so several tasks build on code that already exists there. The detect paths are the extension's agreed file layout after the reorganization: core classes in includes/, each switchable module in modules/<module>/ (not auto-included, so a module that is off loads no code). Hand-edit title/detail/detect freely; set `pin: true` on a task whose status the script should leave alone.

milestones.title: Phase 1 · Contacts and companies
milestones.goal: The record everything else hangs on. A contact is a person with an owner, a lifecycle stage, custom fields and a timeline, linked to companies, sorted by lists, tags and rule-based segments. Privacy, consent and team roles are built in here, once, so no later module can skip them.

tasks.title: Rename to CRM and reorganize
tasks.detail: The Newsletter / Subscriber CRM becomes the CRM: folder `newsletter-crm` becomes `crm`, with its repository, settings, hooks and connector tool names renamed to match (no data to migrate; its tables are already `fw_crm_*`). Its working parts are kept and moved into the new layout rather than rewritten: the email builder, campaigns and the batched sender, lists, tags and segments, double opt-in and the preference page, the contact form action, the Newsletter element listener, the privacy tools and the AI connector tools. Everything that pointed at the old name moves in the same release: the Site Converter, Visitor Insights, the `forms-add` tool and the CRM website generator.

tasks.title: CRM app shell
tasks.detail: The CRM gets its own interface inside wp-admin: a CRM sidebar (Home, Contacts, Companies, Calendar, Deals, Tasks, Campaigns, Automations, Reports, Settings) and a top bar with search and quick add. Opening the CRM folds the WordPress menu to its icons; a focus mode hides it with a **Back to WordPress** link, and a sales rep can land there straight after logging in.

tasks.title: Extension scaffold
tasks.detail: `manifest.php`, the extension class and a settings screen under **Unyson+ → CRM**. Ships inactive; downloaded from the Extensions manager.

tasks.title: Tables and migrations
tasks.detail: Contacts, companies, contact-company links, custom field values, tags and lists, segment definitions and the activity log, each indexed for the screens that read them. Versioned installer with `migrate()`; tables are never dropped on deactivation. Every later change to the tables goes through a numbered migration, so sites update in place. The busiest values (owner, company, lifecycle stage, source, timezone, score, lifetime value, last activity) are real columns on the contact row, so segments stay simple, fast queries.

tasks.title: Modules
tasks.detail: A small core that is always on, and modules switched on from a Modules screen of cards: companies, sales pipeline, calendar, email conversations, email marketing, audit log and webhooks, with automations, scoring and cases to come. A module that is off loads no code and adds no menu; a new site is asked what it will use the CRM for and starts with only that. Other plugins can add their own module.

tasks.title: Contacts
tasks.detail: The subscriber record grows into a contact: an owner, a lifecycle stage (subscriber, lead, customer…), phone and address, companies and custom fields, with subscription status kept as one part of it. A list with search, filters and bulk actions, and a profile page with details, consent, companies, tags, lists and the timeline. Duplicate detection by email.

tasks.title: Companies
tasks.detail: Companies (accounts) with their own fields, owner and timeline; a contact can belong to several.

tasks.title: Custom fields
tasks.detail: Typed fields for contacts, companies and deals, defined on one screen and grouped into sections: text, number, date, choice, money, URL, plus a **lookup** (a link to another record), auto-number, address and calculated fields. Values live in their own table so lists can sort and filter by them.

tasks.title: Tags and lists
tasks.detail: Lists are audiences people join (and leave); tags are labels. Both are the building blocks of segments, automations and membership rules. Carried over from the Newsletter / Subscriber CRM and reworked for the new layout.

tasks.title: Subscription status per list
tasks.detail: Whether someone may be emailed (pending, subscribed, unsubscribed, bounced, complained) is kept per contact and list, with timestamps, separately from the lifecycle stage. Double opt-in, preferences and bounces all depend on it.

tasks.title: Relations between records
tasks.detail: One table of labelled, two-way links between any two records (contact ↔ company, contact ↔ deal, deal ↔ case, a membership ↔ contact), so new record types attach without a schema change.

tasks.title: Activity timeline
tasks.detail: One event log for every contact and company: form submissions, emails, notes, tasks, deal changes, tag changes. Every module writes to it; the profile page reads it.

tasks.title: Rule-based segments
tasks.detail: Segments today hold one filter each (status, list, tag or search). They become saved, live segments built from AND / OR rules over fields, tags, lists, lifecycle stage, activity and dates, feeding campaigns, automations and reports. One filter engine serves list views, segments, campaign audiences, automation conditions and, later, Membership's access rules, so there is one rule language everywhere. Segment counts are cached.

tasks.title: Import and export
tasks.detail: CSV import with column mapping, duplicate handling and a dry run; export of any segment. Carried over from the Newsletter / Subscriber CRM and reworked for the new layout. Every import is a batch that can be rolled back, with saved column mappings; large imports run in the background with a progress bar.

tasks.title: Merge duplicates
tasks.detail: Duplicates suggested on import and on matching email or phone; merging moves tags, lists, deals, notes, the timeline and automation progress onto one record.

tasks.title: Bin and restore
tasks.detail: Deleted records go to a bin first and can be restored; emptying the bin is a separate, explicit step.

tasks.title: Leads from forms
tasks.detail: A contact or booking form adds its senders as contacts: each answer goes to a contact field, an existing custom field or a new one the CRM creates from the form field, the whole submission lands on the timeline, and a booking can become a deal or a meeting. Subscribing still needs a ticked consent box.

tasks.title: Newsletter signup element
tasks.detail: The Newsletter element (in Shortcodes) announces a signup through `fw_newsletter_subscribe`, and the CRM keeps listening to store the contact, with double opt-in when the email module is on. Carried over, so signups never go unsaved during the rename.

tasks.title: Privacy and consent
tasks.detail: A consent log per contact (what, when, from which form), the WordPress personal data exporter and eraser, and retention settings. Carried over from the Newsletter / Subscriber CRM and reworked for the new layout.

tasks.title: Consent log
tasks.detail: What each person agreed to, the exact wording they saw, when, and from which form or page.

tasks.title: Audit log
tasks.detail: Who changed what and when, for admins, built on the same change events every module emits.

tasks.title: Team roles
tasks.detail: CRM capabilities and two roles: a CRM manager sees everything; a sales rep sees and edits only the contacts, companies and deals they own. Every query passes through one permission layer, and creating or linking a WordPress user checks capabilities first.

tasks.title: REST API and AI connector tools
tasks.detail: The REST API grows to every record type, and the AI connector tools (today: describe the set-up, save lists and tags, save segments, settings, draft campaigns) grow to fields, companies and pipelines. No tool returns a contact's personal details.

milestones.title: Phase 2 · Sales pipeline
milestones.goal: Deals on a board. Several pipelines, each with its own stages; deals carry a value, an owner and a close date, and move by drag and drop. Tasks and notes keep the follow-up from slipping.

tasks.title: Pipelines and stages
tasks.detail: Any number of pipelines (sales, onboarding, hiring…), each with ordered stages and a win probability per stage.

tasks.title: Deals
tasks.detail: A deal has a title, value and currency, owner, contacts, company, stage, expected close date and custom fields. Won and lost, with a lost reason. Lost reasons, a per-deal probability that can override the stage's, and stalled-deal alerts when a deal sits in one stage too long.

tasks.title: Pipeline board
tasks.detail: Columns per stage with totals; drag a deal to move it, to won or to lost. Filters by owner, value and date.

tasks.title: Deal page
tasks.detail: Details, contacts, company, tasks, notes and the deal's timeline on one screen.

tasks.title: Tasks and reminders
tasks.detail: Calls, meetings, emails and to-dos with due dates and owners, on contacts, companies and deals; a My Tasks view and email reminders.

tasks.title: Notes
tasks.detail: Notes on any record, shown on its timeline.

tasks.title: REST API for deals, pipelines and tasks
tasks.detail: Pipelines, deals (move, win, lose, the bin, linked contacts, the timeline), tasks and notes through the CRM's REST API, with the same rules as the screens: a sales rep reaches only their own deals and tasks.

tasks.title: Calls, meetings and calendar
tasks.detail: Log calls (outcome, duration, notes) and schedule meetings with a time, attendees and a reminder; a calendar view of everything due.

tasks.title: Files on records
tasks.detail: Attach files from the media library to contacts, companies and deals.

tasks.title: Products and line items
tasks.detail: Optional: line items on deals from a simple product list, or from WooCommerce products when it is active. A line item copies the price, so later price changes do not rewrite old deals.

tasks.title: One-to-one email
tasks.detail: Write to a contact from their profile or a deal; the email is sent through the Mailer and logged on the timeline.

tasks.title: Replies on the timeline
tasks.detail: Replies reach the contact's timeline through a BCC address or a connected mailbox, which also lets an automation stop when someone answers.

tasks.title: Sales reports
tasks.detail: Pipeline value by stage, a forecast weighted by stage probability, won and lost over time, and performance per owner.

tasks.title: CRM home dashboard
tasks.detail: Counts, tasks due today, deals by stage, recent activity, list growth and the health of the sending queue, as cards you can rearrange.

milestones.title: Phase 2b · Cases
milestones.goal: Support requests tracked like deals. A case belongs to a contact and company, moves through statuses, has a priority and an owner, and keeps every reply and note on the timeline.

tasks.title: Cases
tasks.detail: A light support-ticket record with its own statuses (new, open, waiting on the customer, solved), a priority, an owner and a due date. The conversation lives on the case timeline.

tasks.title: Case list and board
tasks.detail: A list and a board by status, filtered by owner, priority and age.

tasks.title: Cases from forms and email
tasks.detail: A contact form action and the inbound email address can open a case.

milestones.title: Phase 3 · Email marketing
milestones.goal: Campaigns that reach the inbox. Designed in a block email builder from a template gallery, sent in batches through SMTP or an email service, and measured with opens and clicks.

tasks.title: Sending queue
tasks.detail: Campaigns are queued and sent in small batches by the scheduler, so a big send never hits a host's time limit, with per-hour limits to respect shared hosting. Carried over from the Newsletter / Subscriber CRM and reworked for the new layout. One queue row per recipient, claimed atomically so no email is ever sent twice; a sending-rate cap with presets per kind of host; a per-campaign speed limit so opens and clicks cannot flood the site; the per-recipient send log cleared after a retention period while each campaign's totals are kept.

tasks.title: Email services
tasks.detail: Campaigns and CRM email can be sent through SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, Brevo or Amazon SES by API instead of the site mail, chosen per sender, with each service's bounce, complaint and unsubscribe webhook feeding back into the CRM.

tasks.title: Email builder
tasks.detail: Drag-and-drop blocks (text, image, button, columns, social, divider) compiled to email-safe HTML, with personalization tags and a live preview. Carried over from the Newsletter / Subscriber CRM and reworked for the new layout.

tasks.title: Template gallery
tasks.detail: Ready-made starters (announcement, newsletter digest, promotion, welcome, follow-up, event invitation, plain letter), plus saving your own from the builder.

tasks.title: Campaigns
tasks.detail: Pick an audience (list, tag or segment), design, test, schedule and send. Campaigns that have started can no longer be edited, so everyone gets the same email. Carried over from the Newsletter / Subscriber CRM and reworked for the new layout.

tasks.title: Double opt-in and preferences
tasks.detail: Confirmation emails, a preference page where people choose their lists, and one-click unsubscribe in every email. Carried over from the Newsletter / Subscriber CRM and reworked for the new layout.

tasks.title: Opens, clicks and bounces
tasks.detail: Open and click tracking (switchable, for privacy), bounce and complaint handling, and campaign reports. Clicks from corporate link scanners are filtered out, and tracked links are stored once in a short-link table.

tasks.title: Sender profiles
tasks.detail: Several From names and addresses, and transactional email (receipts, confirmations) kept apart from marketing email.

tasks.title: Smart links and post digests
tasks.detail: Links that add a tag when clicked, and a recurring email of the latest posts.

tasks.title: Message channels
tasks.detail: Email is the first channel of a channel registry, so SMS and messaging apps can be added later without changing campaigns or automations.

milestones.title: Phase 4 · Automations
milestones.goal: The CRM working on its own. An automation starts on a trigger and runs steps: send an email, wait, branch on a condition, change tags, move a deal, create a task, call a webhook. Built to run reliably on ordinary shared hosting.

tasks.title: Automation engine
tasks.detail: Each contact's progress through an automation is a row with a next-run time; the runner processes due rows in small batches. Waits of minutes or months cost nothing while they wait.

tasks.title: Reliable scheduling
tasks.detail: A health check that shows whether the scheduler is running on time, and the exact cron line for a real server cron job (cPanel and similar), replacing WordPress's visit-triggered scheduler.

tasks.title: Triggers
tasks.detail: Form submitted, list joined or left, tag added or removed, field changed, date reached (birthdays, renewals), deal stage changed, email opened or clicked, purchase made.

tasks.title: Actions
tasks.detail: Send an email, wait, if / else, add or remove tags and lists, update a field, create or move a deal, create a task, notify the team, call a webhook, start or end another automation.

tasks.title: Goals and exit conditions
tasks.detail: Jump ahead when a contact reaches a goal (buys, books, replies), and leave an automation when a condition stops being true.

tasks.title: Automation editor
tasks.detail: A visual flow editor: triggers at the top, steps in between, branches side by side, with a count of contacts at each step.

tasks.title: Ready-made automations
tasks.detail: Welcome series, lead nurture, quote or booking follow-up, re-engagement and deal follow-up, ready to switch on and edit.

tasks.title: Run log and contact progress
tasks.detail: Each run is logged as succeeded, partly done or failed with the reason, and every contact shows which automations they are in and at which step.

tasks.title: Safe automations
tasks.detail: A loop guard so automations cannot set each other off endlessly, a once-per-contact option, edits staged on live automations so people already inside are not broken, and a test run for one contact.

tasks.title: More conditions and steps
tasks.detail: Changed to / changed from conditions, date and birthday triggers, a random split, and round-robin owner assignment.

tasks.title: Command line
tasks.detail: WP-CLI commands to run the sending queue and automations, the scaling path on a VPS.

milestones.title: Phase 5 · Scoring and site activity
milestones.goal: Know who is ready to buy. Points for what contacts do, and which pages known contacts read, so the team calls the warmest leads first.

tasks.title: Lead scoring
tasks.detail: Rules that add or remove points for opens, clicks, page visits, form submissions and fields; scores that fade over time; segments and automations by score. Several named scores per contact (by product or interest) and a score on deals.

tasks.title: Site activity for known contacts
tasks.detail: Pages a contact visits after they identify themselves (a form or an email click), with consent, on their timeline and as an automation trigger.

tasks.title: Events
tasks.detail: One events table for anything a contact does (custom events from code, clicks on marked elements, logins, purchases), usable in segments, scores and automations.

milestones.title: Phase 6 · Integrations and the extension API
milestones.goal: Other extensions build on the CRM without reaching into its tables. A documented, versioned PHP API, events and REST endpoints let the Membership extension, WooCommerce and anything written later read and change contacts, tags and deals, and react when they change.

tasks.title: Public PHP API
tasks.detail: One entry point, `fw_crm()`, for finding, creating and updating contacts, companies and deals, adding and removing tags and lists, checking membership of a tag, list or segment, and writing to the timeline. Versioned and documented; the tables behind it stay private.

tasks.title: Events catalogue
tasks.detail: A documented action for every change (contact created, tag added, list joined, deal moved, email clicked…), each with the same payload shape, so integrations and automations listen to one stream.

tasks.title: Outbound webhooks
tasks.detail: Send CRM events (new contacts, tags, subscriptions, deals won, tasks done, email opens, clicks and bounces) to other apps as signed JSON the moment they happen, retried in the background and logged, with a test button and a REST API to manage them. Other extensions add their own events.

tasks.title: Integrations registry
tasks.detail: Extensions register themselves as CRM integrations: their own triggers and actions appear in Automations, their own fields on the contact page, and their activity on the timeline. The CRM never needs to know about them in advance.

tasks.title: WooCommerce
tasks.detail: Customers become contacts; orders, totals and products land on the timeline and become segment rules and automation triggers (purchased, refunded, abandoned cart).

tasks.title: Ready for the Membership extension
tasks.detail: Membership is its own extension. The CRM gives it what it needs: a contact linked to a WordPress user only when someone must log in, tag, list and segment checks for access rules, and membership events (joined, renewed, expired) on the timeline and in Automations.

tasks.title: Dashboard widget registry
tasks.detail: Other extensions add their own cards to the CRM home dashboard.

tasks.title: Purchase summaries
tasks.detail: Each store or membership provider keeps a summary per contact (orders, total spent, plan and status), so segments and automations can use it without reaching into other extensions' tables.

tasks.title: Custom objects
tasks.detail: An API for registering new record types (with fields, relations, the timeline and permissions), with an admin screen later.

milestones.title: Phase 7 · Built with AI
milestones.goal: The whole CRM can be set up by an AI app through the connector, and the CRM website generator builds sites on it.

tasks.title: Connector tools for every module
tasks.detail: Pipelines and stages, campaigns and templates, automations from recipes, scoring rules and access rules, each as an AI Assistant tool. Setting things up, never reading or contacting the people in the CRM.

tasks.title: CRM website generator on the CRM
tasks.detail: The generator's prompts build on the CRM: a real pipeline instead of stage tags, and a welcome automation instead of a single welcome email.
